## `labs/flow/for_each` { #labs-flow-for_each }

Run a nested list of steps once for every item of a list.

The nested steps resolve their `with:` when they run, not when the loop starts, which is what lets them read `${{ each.item }}`. The loop stops at the first nested failure and fails with it; a step that reports an outcome instead of failing — a delete answering 404 — keeps it going.

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Also accepts | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of any | yes | — | — | The values to loop over, usually a list a previous step returned. An empty list runs nothing and passes. |
| `steps` | list of [StepDefinition](#stepdefinition) | yes | — | — | Nested step definitions run once per item, in order — the same shape used at the top level of a test. They read the current item as '${{ each.item }}' and its position, from 0, as '${{ each.index }}'. |

**Output** — the value assertions and `returns:` read

_How many items the loop ran for, and what each run produced._

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `iterations` | integer | Number of items the nested steps ran for. |
| `outputs` | list of list of any | Per item, in order, the outputs of the nested steps. |
